newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus police arrest four for deadly dog fights.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus police arrest four for deadly dog fights.

text.p: Four people have been arrested in Cyprus on suspicion of holding deadly dog fights for betting, police said on Friday.
Scenes of a fight involving a pit bull and an alsatian dripping in blood and gnashing at one another's throats were first shown on television on Wednesday night.

"Police have gathered sufficient evidence which has helped inquiries," police spokesman Glafcos Xenos told Reuters, adding that investigations have been extended from the south eastern Larnaca district to include the southern district of Limassol.
Two of the suspects own pit bull terriers and the third, a farmer, has a number of dogs, Xenos said.
The private Antenna station said the fight was organised for betting and the footage was shot in the Larnaca district.
It prompted a barrage of protest calls to the government veterinary department when the same scenes were shown on Thursday evening.
Cruelty to animals is punishable by up to six months in jail for first-time offenders or a 500 pound ($980) fine. The penalities are doubled for repeat offenders.
The import of pit bull terriers and three other breeds are banned under new legislation, which classes them as "dangerous", Pavlos Economides, the director of the island's veterinary department said.
But a number of these animals were in Cyprus, imported before legislation came into effect. Economides was non-commital when asked what would be done with them.
"We look after animal welfare and a dog is a man's best friend. Of course we wouldn't favour the option of putting them to sleep," he said.
Last year animal rights groups expressed concern at indications they had of dog fights taking place, but at the time police said they had insufficient evidence to merit prosecution.
